newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex called lower, spot month expires.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex called lower, spot month expires.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures were expected to open 20 to 25 cents a barrel lower while products were seen down 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon as the complex continues to step down from the heights scaled last week.
Traders said a lack of special features in products would keep heating oil and unleaded gas tied to crude oil.

Crude oil futures will spend the session completing the expiration of the June contract. Traders said liquidation and rollovers would again capture most crude action, as it did on Monday, and said the spot contract could see a fair amount of producer selling into it.
Open interest in June stood at about 32,325 lots at the start of the session.
Early talk of this afternoon's American Petroleum Institute inventory figures mostly foresaw mixed to flat numbers compared with last week's suprisingly large rise in stocks.
"We're looking for flat to higher in distillate, flat in gasoline, and crude stocks easier," one floor analyst said.
Support for July WTI, which settled Monday's NYMEX trade at $21.90, was seen at $21.16.
